# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s147) | **#890 ROUND 2 @ `4096bdd1a` — three items done, 149→166 green, AND IT REFUTED WEDNESDAY'S FIX INSTRUCTION IN THREE PLACES WITH MEASUREMENTS** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The refutation is the score.** Wednesday specified base64url as the F2/F3 fix, asserting it removed the `-` sentinel. It measured `base64url('-') == 'LQ'` and showed the collision survives — *"encoding a sentinel renames it, it does not remove it"* — with a three-row table (`cur` / `keep` / `no`) making the before, the instructed fix and the correct fix comparable at a glance. **It then found the second-order error: a total encoder ALONE creates a FRESH collision class** (`b64('\ud800') == b64('\ud801') == b64('\ufffd') == "77-9"`) — **which is Wednesday's own objection to a try/catch, applied to Wednesday's own fix.** **And a third: Wednesday's two instructions in one mail could not both hold** — the wire cell Wednesday specified returns 200, not 400, under Wednesday's own fix; its boundary refusal is what makes Wednesday's cell true as written. **F5: it refused to inherit Wednesday's figure of four.** It tampered each candidate ALONE against the 149-cell baseline and found its own first four were not the right four (C3 already covered); **four controls DID red**, so the instrument discriminates. C2 is the KS-882 lesson exactly — `sweepExpired` unit-tested with nothing asserting the route calls it. **Every new cell red-proofed individually, never as a set; every file restored byte-identical (`diff -q` clean ×3); suite back to 166 green after each.** **Disclosed an unasked change** — a pre-existing cell its encoding broke — and **updated rather than deleted it, re-deriving the expectation INDEPENDENTLY in the test rather than by calling the module under test**, plus a `not.toContain` so a revert reds. **Conceded the priority argument cleanly** (*"I have nothing to say back on that"*) **while refusing the technical one — separating those two is the whole skill.** Merge left HELD; no deploy; platform suites not run with its reason stated for Wednesday to judge rather than inherit. |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-952 / PR #890 @ `74c0b3bbf`, TIER 1 round 1) | **GO-with-findings, and it HANDED WEDNESDAY THE LEVER instead of taking it** — *"severity is mine, priority is not"* | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **F1 fix-shape demonstrated END-TO-END and the worktree restored**, with the repo's own gate red-proofed BOTH directions (tamper the yaml → FAIL; tamper the generator without regenerating → FAIL) — which is how it proved the omission is in the GENERATOR, not artefact drift, since the gate passes today. **F2 driven at the WIRE with controls** (identical request with an ordinary value → 200, so the cell measures the surrogate and not a broken route), and it verified the value is transmissible by round-tripping `\ud800` through express's own parser. **Named F2 a REGRESSION** — neither route called `encodeURIComponent` at the base SHA. **Reachability stated honestly in BOTH directions** — `/reset` platform-gated, `/check` near-unreachable because the minters take claims from Postgres — so severity was not inflated. **F3 found the `-` sentinel reachable, i.e. the join non-injective in a corner, while stating plainly that nothing it found reopens the collision the PR exists to close.** F6 marked observation-only, no action. |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-597 / PR #889 @ `af640e809`, tier 2 + the MANDATED real-Postgres leg) | **GO-with-findings — and the mandated leg found TWO things no mocked cell could reach, which is the whole argument for naming it

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
